keyframe_review.note: 82,885 km2 around Gwalior and Malwa (300 Madhya Pradesh cells) for 1820-1841 is not the Maratha Empire, which ended in 1818 ('Dissolution of the Marathas: 1818', infobox). After the Third Anglo-Maratha War 'Gwalior (Shinde)' became 'a princely state acknowledging British control' and Holkar's Indore a subsidiary state. The shape belongs to the successor Gwalior (Scindia) state, whose dossier is not in this batch.

correction.text: not used for the Maratha Empire; the same cells belong to the Gwalior (Shinde) princely state from 1818

correction.text: not used for the Maratha Empire; belongs to the Gwalior (Shinde) princely state

ledger.note: 1674: Shivaji is crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad. 'On 6 June 1674, Shivaji was crowned king of the Maratha Empire'; a second coronation followed on 24 September 1674. The infobox of the Maratha Empire page gives 'Coronation of Shivaji: 6 June 1674'. The page names forts, not a boundary.

region.text: the forts around Raigad, Pune and Satara

ledger.note: April 1675: Shivaji takes Ponda from Bijapur ('capturing the Bijapuri forts of Ponda (April 1675), Karwar (mid-year), and Kolhapur (July)').
July 1675: Kolhapur and Karwar pass from Bijapur to the Marathas. This is the southern patch Cliopatria draws from 1677.

1677: Shivaji invades the Karnataka and seizes Vellore and Gingee. 'In 1677, Shivaji invaded Karnataka with 30,000 cavalry and 40,000 infantry', backed by a treaty with the Qutbshah of Golkonda; he 'seized the forts of Vellore and Gingee'. The page gives no capture date and does not name the previous holder; Bijapur is my reading (Bijapur's Cliopatria neighbour list touches the Marathas to 1686).

region.text: the forts of Vellore and Gingee

ledger.note: 26 November 1677: Shivaji defeats his half-brother Venkoji and takes his Mysore-plateau holdings. 'defeated his half-brother's army on 26 November 1677' and 'seized most of his possessions on the Mysore plateau'; a settlement then returned many properties to Venkoji's family (undated, so the land stays Maratha here; thanjavur-maratha-kingdom is the half-brother's state). Counterpart is Bijapur on the map, whose Cliopatria shape held the Bangalore country.

region.text: most of Venkoji's possessions on the Mysore plateau

ledger.note: 1680: the Mughal-Maratha (Deccan) wars begin. Infobox 'Deccan Wars: 1680-1707'; 'In 1681, Sambhaji succeeded after his father's death. Aurangzeb headed south the same year.' The page gives no frontier; the zone is Maharashtra as mughal-empire's dossier draws it.

region.text: the Maratha country of the western Deccan

ledger.note: 1689: Sambhaji is captured (1 February) and executed (21 March); Rajaram takes the court south to Jinji, 'Jinji: 1689-1698 (de facto)' in the infobox. The Mughal-Maratha Wars page: 'Rajaram travelled south under escort of Khando Ballal' (no year).
January 1698: Jinji falls to the Mughals; the page says Jinji 'fell in January 1698'. Cliopatria's shape does not draw Jinji (its 1677-1690 shapes stop short of Tamil Nadu).
1700: Rajaram dies at Sinhagad (March 1700) and Tarabai rules for her son; the infobox gives 'Satara: 1700-1818 (royal seat)'.

April 1700: Satara surrenders to Aurangzeb. 'Surrendered in April 1700, just before the onset of the monsoon.' The page does not date the Maratha recovery of Satara, yet the infobox keeps it as the royal seat from 1700.

1706: the Mughals start to leave Maratha land. 'In 1706, Mughals started retreating from Maratha dominions'; earlier 'In 1705, two Maratha army factions crossed Narmada' and 'By 1705 end, Marathas had penetrated Mughal possession of Central India and Gujarat'. The extent regained is my reading (Cliopatria's 1718 core).

region.text: the Maratha dominions the Mughals left

ledger.note: 21 February 1707: Aurangzeb dies and the long Mughal war ends de facto. 'He died of a fever on 21 February 1707' (the page's quoted sources disagree: Marshman gives 27 February); Shahu was then released by Bahadur Shah I.

region.text: the Maratha country of the western Deccan

ledger.note: 1707: the Maratha house divides. 'Two rival seats were set up in 1707, at Satara (Shahu) and Kolhapur (Tarabai)'. The page lists a Kolhapur line of Chhatrapatis (Shivaji II 1700-1714, Sambhaji II 1714-1760, Shivaji III 1760-1812); whether Kolhapur is a separate state or a branch of the empire is a modelling choice (notes). [fx-43 R078] Dated 1710 (was 1707): the Kolhapur State page has 'Established: 1710' in its infobox, 'The states of Satara and Kolhapur came into being in 1707, because of the succession dispute over the Maratha throne' in its text, and 'By 1710, two separate principalities had become an established fact'; the kolhapur-state dossier is founded in 1710 (its ledger/0, counterpart maratha-empire), so a 1707 split left the Kolhapur cells nobody's for three years. Until 1710 the Kolhapur seat is inside the one Maratha realm (patch p1700-p1709 keyframe_overrides/6 draws it so for the 1707 keyframe).

16 November 1713: Balaji Vishwanath is appointed Peshwa. The state continues under the same colour but power passes from the Chhatrapati to the Peshwas (Balaji Vishwanath 1713-1720; Baji Rao I 1720-1740; Balaji Baji Rao 1740-1761 and so on).

1719: the Marathas march to Delhi and depose Farrukhsiyar, and Shahu is granted possession of Shivaji's 1680 territory. 'Shahu was granted chauth and sardeshmukhi from the six Mughal Deccan provinces, and possession of the territory Shivaji held in 1680.' The chauth provinces are tribute, not drawn; the land is my reading (Cliopatria's 1721 shape).

1728: the Peshwa's seat is Poona (infobox 'Poona: 1728-1818'); the same year Baji Rao I beat the Nizam at Palkhed (28 February in this page, 25 February in the Baji Rao I page) and the Nizam signed the Treaty of Mungi Shevgaon on 6 March recognising Shahu and the Maratha tax rights.

1730: a Maratha force under Chimaji Appa goes into Gujarat ('sent a Maratha force under Chimaji Appa there in 1730'); at Dabhoi in 1731 Baji Rao I beat the rebel Maratha Trimbak Rao Dabhade. The page does not name the Mughal governor; the opponent and the span are my reading.

1731: Chhatrasal leaves the Marathas a third of Bundelkhand. 'Before Chhatrasal's death in December 1731, he ceded one-third of his territories to the Marathas' after Baji Rao I's March 1729 march to Bundelkhand with 25,000 horsemen.

25 September 1736: the Siddis of Janjira are shut in. A peace treaty 'confined them to Janjira, Gowalkot and Anjanvel' (the 1733 treaty had left them Janjira, Anjanvel, Gowalkot and Underi, while the Marathas kept Raigad, Rewas, Thal and Chaul).

region.text: the Konkan coast except Janjira, Gowalkot and Anjanvel

ledger.note: 1738: Gujarat is Maratha. Cliopatria's 1738 shape is the first with Gujarat (364 of 772 cells); the pages opened date the 1730 force and the 1731 Dabhoi battle but not the consolidation, so the end of the contest is a bridge.
1738: Gujarat enters the Maratha shape. A bridging date from Cliopatria's 1738 shape; the Maratha Empire page credits Gujarat to Khanderao Dabhade and Triambakrao without a date.

1738: the Marathas attack Bassein. 'Five years later [than the planned attack on Salsette of 13 March 1733] the Marathas would again invade Portuguese territory and attack Bassein.' The page gives no outcome and no date: the year is 1733 plus five and the capture is inferred from the 1775 treaty in which Raghunathrao cedes Salsette and Bassein to the British. A gap-filler should open the Battle of Vasai article.

7 January 1738: the Treaty of Bhopal gives Malwa to the Marathas. 'Malwa was ceded to the Marathas' and the Mughals paid Rs 5,000,000; Baji Rao had been deputy governor of Malwa since 4 March 1736 (Kishangad) and crossed the Narmada in early December 1737.

region.text: Malwa, ceded by the Treaty of Bhopal

ledger.note: 1739: Khargone and Handia are ceded. After the clash with Nasir Jung 'Khargone and Handia were formally ceded to the Maratha Empire'; the Marathas gave up their chauth rights in the six Deccan provinces and Baji Rao I promised not to invade the Deccan again (the page's accounts of the battle conflict).

1740: Raghuji Bhonsle's army enters the Carnatic. 'Carnatic (Raghuji Bhonsle): Damalcherry in 1740; Arcot taken'; the Carnatic Sultanate page: 'In 1740, the Maratha forces descended on Arcot' and Dost Ali Khan died at Damalcherry.

14 March 1741: Trichinopoly surrenders and the Carnatic expedition ends. The page says only that Trichinopoly surrendered on 14 March 1741; the Maratha garrison at Trichinopoly and its end are not on any page opened (notes), so the land is not drawn as Maratha.

April 1742: Bhaskar Ram's Marathas invade Bengal through Orissa. 'In April, Maratha forces under Bhaskar Ram sent by Raghuji Bhonsle to collect chauth tribute, invaded Bengal via Odisha'; Barabati Fort at Cuttack was captured on 19 April 1742. They left Bengal on 17 September 1742; Raghuji occupied Burdwan in 1743; Orissa was occupied again in 1745 and Cuttack recaptured in June 1749.

1751: the Subarnarekha becomes the frontier. The treaty was 'formally signed with the approval of the Nagpur court in May or June 1751': Rs 1,200,000 a year as the chauth of Bengal and Bihar from October 1751, and 'the territories beyond the Subarnarekha River near Jalasore' fixed as the boundary of the Bengal subah.

1752: Orissa is formally incorporated. 'Thus de facto Maratha control over Orissa was established by 1751, while de jure it remained a part of Bengal Subah till 1752. After the assassination of Mir Habib, the governor of Orissa, in 1752, the Marathas formally incorporated Orissa in their dominion.'
August 1757: Raghunath Rao takes Delhi. 'Raghunath Rao took Delhi in August 1757.' The page does not say from whom; the Afghan garrison named for 1760 suggests it was lost again before August 1760.
8 May 1758: Peshawar falls to the Marathas in the Afghan-Maratha war (infobox 8 March 1758 - 14 January 1761). The Durrani dossier opens its own contest in 1759 at Lahore.

3 January 1760: Sadashivrao Bhau beats Salabat Jung at Udgir. 'The aftermath of the war resulted in the Nizam's forces surrendering territory worth 60 lakhs, including the cities of Ahmadnagar, Daultabad, Burhanpur and Bijapur.' The page does not state that the Marathas took the land; Cliopatria draws it from 1762.
August 1760: Delhi is retaken. 'Delhi was recaptured from the Afghan garrison in August 1760.'

14 January 1761: the Marathas lose the Third Battle of Panipat and the northwest. The page states the defeat; the Punjab ends as a Maratha claim (Durrani dossier: 'The Durranis decisively defeated the Marathas').
January 1761: Delhi passes out of Maratha hands after Panipat. The page does not date the loss; it is inferred from the statement that Mahadaji Shinde had to recapture Delhi in early 1771.

Early 1771: Mahadaji Shinde recaptures Delhi ('Mahadaji Shinde recaptured Delhi in early 1771'). The page does not say who held it; Cliopatria adds Delhi and the Doab to the Maratha shape in 1772. Rohilkhand ('captured in 1752, at Safdarjung's request', devastated after 1772) is not modelled: the pages do not date a Maratha tenure.

1 March 1776: the Treaty of Purandar annuls the Treaty of Surat (6 March 1775, Raghunathrao ceded 'Salsette and Bassein' and part of the Surat and Bharuch revenues) but 'the revenues of Salsette and Bharuch districts were retained by the British'. Salbai (17 May 1782) confirmed it: 'The Marathas accepted the British cession of Salsette and Bassein by Raghunathrao.'

15 February 1779: Goddard captures Ahmedabad (after the Treaty of Wadgaon of 16 January 1779, which the Bengal government rejected). 'Captured Ahmedabad on 15 February 1779'; Gwalior fell on 4 August 1780 (Popham, helped by the Rana of Gohad) and Bassein on 11 December 1780 (Goddard).

region.text: Ahmedabad, Gwalior and Bassein, the three places the British took

ledger.note: 17 May 1782: the Treaty of Salbai ends the First Anglo-Maratha War. 'Both sides returned territory captured during the war'; the British recognised Maratha claims west of the Jumna and the Marathas recognised British suzerainty over the Nawab of Arcot (ratified June 1782 and February 1783).

region.text: the places taken in the war

ledger.note: 1783: Gwalior is conquered. 'In 1783, Mahadaji besieged the fort of Gwalior and conquered it'; the fort 'was then in the hands of Chhatar Singh, the Jat ruler of Gohad' (quote corrected by reviewer sa-05-d). The Rana of Gohad had held it with the British since 4 August 1780 (First Anglo-Maratha War page).

8 August 1803: Wellesley storms the Ahmednagar pettah (the fort surrenders on 12 August). The Treaty of Bassein (December 1802) had made the Peshwa a British subsidiary; Delhi fell in September, Assaye 23 September, Laswari in November and Argaon on 29 November 1803.

region.text: the lands lost in 1803: Ahmednagar, Haryana, the Doab and Delhi, Cuttack, Broach

ledger.note: September 1803: Lake beats Scindia at Delhi. 'In September 1803, Scindia forces lost to Lake at Delhi' (the Maratha Empire page: 'the Marathas lost influence over Delhi').

17 December 1803: Bhonsle gives up Cuttack. 'On 17 December 1803, Raghoji II Bhonsale of Nagpur signed the Treaty of Deogaon'; he gave up 'the province of Cuttack, which included the coastal part of Odisha, Balasore Port, and parts of Midnapore district'.

region.text: the province of Cuttack, Balasore and part of Midnapore

ledger.note: 30 December 1803: Scindia signs the Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon and cedes the northern conquests, Broach and Ahmadnagar. The page lists 'Hisar, Panipat, Rohtak, Rewari, Gurgaon, Ganges-Jamuna Doab', 'parts of Bundelkhand, Broach, some districts of Gujarat and the fort of Ahmadnagar'. Bundelkhand and the Agra part are only named in this text.

region.text: Hisar, Panipat, Rohtak, Rewari, Gurgaon, the Ganges-Jamuna Doab, the Delhi-Agra region, parts of Bundelkhand, Broach, some Gujarat districts and Ahmadnagar

ledger.note: 30 December 1803: the war with Scindia and Bhonsle ends by treaty; hostilities against Holkar began on 6 April 1804 and ended with the Treaty of Rajghat.
24 December 1805: Holkar signs the Treaty of Rajghat and gives up Tonk, Rampura and Bundi to the British.

13 June 1817: the Treaty of Poona. The Peshwa 'had to give up his most important Deccan strongholds, the Konkan seaboard, and all places north of the Narmada and south of the Tungabhadra'. Only the Konkan is drawn here; the other clauses name no district.

region.text: the Konkan seaboard, the Deccan strongholds, and all places north of the Narmada and south of the Tungabhadra

ledger.note: 5 November 1817: war breaks out at Khadki, the same day as the Treaty of Gwalior. Mahidpur 21 December 1817 (Holkar's force destroyed), the Nagpur defenders left on 30 December, Koregaon 1 January 1818.

region.text: Pune, Nagpur and Malwa, where the war was fought

ledger.note: 5 November 1817: the Treaty of Gwalior. 'Shinde surrendered Rajasthan (Rajputana), ceded his armed forces and major forts, and agreed to help fight the Pindaris.'

9 January 1818: the Nagpur treaty. Appa Saheb kept nominal rule 'under restrictions' while 'most of his territory, including forts, came under British control'; the Treaty of Mandeswar (6 January 1818) made Holkar's state subsidiary.

region.text: Bhonsle's territory: 'most of his territory, including forts'

ledger.note: 3 June 1818: the Peshwa surrenders and is sent to Bithur near Kanpur. Fighting went on until Asirgarh fell on 9 April 1819.

1818: the Maratha Empire is dissolved. 'Most [of the Peshwa's territories] were annexed into the Bombay Presidency', Bundelkhand became the Saugor and Nerbudda Territories, Satara was restored as a princely state under Pratap Singh (annexed 1848), and the Shinde, Holkar and Bhonsle states survived as British protectorates. Infobox: 'Dissolution of the Marathas: 1818'.

region.text: the Peshwa's territories, annexed into the Bombay Presidency

wars.name: Mughal-Maratha Wars

zones.text: the Maratha country of the western Deccan

wars.outcome: Aurangzeb took Bijapur by September 1686, captured Sambhaji on 1 February 1689, took Jinji in January 1698 and Satara in April 1700, but died on 21 February 1707 with the Marathas under Tarabai raiding across the Narmada; Shahu was released and the Maratha house divided.
wars.note: The page gives no frontier. The Mughal dossier and this one use the same zone (Maharashtra) and close it in 1707.

wars.name: Battle of Palkhed
wars.outcome: Baji Rao I beat the Nizam on 25 or 28 February 1728; by the Treaty of Mungi Shevgaon (6 March) the Nizam recognised Shahu and the Maratha tax rights in the Deccan. No territory is stated.
wars.note: The Maratha Empire page gives 28 February 1728, the Baji Rao I page 25 February.

wars.name: Maratha-Siddi wars of Janjira
wars.outcome: The 1733 treaty left the Siddis Janjira, Anjanvel, Gowalkot and Underi; the peace of 25 September 1736 confined them to Janjira, Gowalkot and Anjanvel.

wars.name: Maratha conquest of Malwa and Battle of Bhopal
wars.outcome: Deputy governor of Malwa from 4 March 1736; Delhi outskirts 28 March 1737; Bhopal in December 1737; the treaty of 7 January 1738 ceded Malwa and Rs 5,000,000.

wars.name: Maratha invasions of Bengal
wars.outcome: Six expeditions (Maratha Empire page: 1741-1748; the Bengal page covers 1742-1752) ended with the 1751 treaty: Rs 1,200,000 a year chauth, the Subarnarekha as boundary, Orissa incorporated in 1752.
wars.note: Page conflicts: Bhaskar Pant is both 'killed in action' and fleeing Katwa on 27 September 1742; the Maratha Empire page puts the expeditions at 1741-1748.

wars.name: Maratha invasion of the Carnatic
wars.outcome: Raghuji Bhonsle beat and killed Dost Ali at Damalcherry in 1740, Arcot was taken, Trichinopoly surrendered on 14 March 1741.
wars.note: Neither the Carnatic Sultanate page nor the Carnatic Wars page dates the Maratha garrison at Trichinopoly or its end.

wars.name: Afghan-Maratha War (Third Battle of Panipat)
wars.outcome: Peshawar fell to the Marathas on 8 May 1758; the Marathas lost the Third Battle of Panipat on 14 January 1761 and the north-west.

wars.name: Battle of Udgir
wars.outcome: Sadashivrao Bhau beat Salabat Jung on 3 January 1760; the Nizam surrendered territory worth 60 lakhs.

wars.name: Maratha-Mysore wars

zones.text: the country between the Krishna and the Tungabhadra

wars.outcome: Madhavrao I crossed the Krishna in 1767 and beat Hyder Ali at Sira and Madgiri; the infobox gives August 1768 - April 1787 and the Treaty of Gajendragad of April 1787. No cession is on the page opened.
wars.note: Unverified: page budget. The Maratha table entry for 1798 puts the frontier at the Tungabhadra after 1795.

wars.name: First Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: Inconclusive; the Treaty of Salbai (17 May 1782) returned the territory captured in the war, the British keeping Salsette.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: British victory: Deogaon (17 December 1803) and Surji-Anjangaon (30 December 1803) ceded Cuttack, Haryana, the Doab, Delhi-Agra, parts of Bundelkhand, Broach and Ahmadnagar; Rajghat (24 December 1805) took Tonk, Rampura and Bundi from Holkar.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War
wars.outcome: The Peshwa's territories were annexed into the Bombay Presidency, the Bhonsle lost most of Nagpur, Holkar and Shinde became British subsidiaries; Satara was restored as a princely state; Asirgarh fell on 9 April 1819.

certainty.note: Hill forts and raided districts: the pages give forts and cities, not boundaries. The only line fixed by treaty in these years is the Siddi limit of 25 September 1736 on the Konkan coast.
Chauth and sphere-of-influence land is not territory. Exception: the Subarnarekha frontier with Bengal fixed in 1751 is sharp.
The British treaty cessions of 1803, 1805 and 1817-1818 name districts and are sharp; the lines between the Peshwa, Scindia, Holkar, Gaekwad and Bhonsle remain soft.

notes:
Nine pages opened (budget: up to 9). Cliopatria's 'Maratha Empire' row is read as one state, 1674 (coronation) to June 1818, with the Peshwa-era confederacy as a 'rename' in 1713; the 1820-1845 shapes (82,885 km2 around Gwalior/Malwa) are marked wrong and belong to the Gwalior (Shinde) princely state.

What the shapes are: the 1677-1690 shape is only the Kolhapur / south Konkan / Karwar patch (no cell near Pune, one near Satara, none at Vellore or Bangalore), the 1718 shape is a Satara core, from 1721 the shapes are the Peshwa's heartland; the infobox's 2.5 M km2 for 1760 is 2.1-2.5 times the shape and counts tribute and raided lands (kept as sphere of influence, not drawn).

Not settled:
- The gap 1691-1717 (no Cliopatria shape) is bridged with confidence-1 keyframes from the 1687 and 1718 shapes; the pages give only losses (Jinji 1698, Satara 1700), not holdings. A gap-filler should read 'Tarabai', 'Shahu I' and 'Treaty of Lonavala'.
- Kolhapur: split recorded in 1707 on the page's 'two rival seats'; whether it is a state of its own (a Kolhapur dossier is listed under counterparts_needing_dossiers) is a modelling choice.
- Chauth is not modelled as vassalage: the 1719 grant from the six Mughal Deccan provinces, the Bengal and Bihar chauth of 1751 and the Peshwa's 1802 subsidiary alliance (Treaty of Bassein, December 1802, territory unnamed) are in notes only.
- Salsette and Bassein: the Marathas took them from the Portuguese (page: 'five years later' than 1733; no outcome) - gain at confidence 1 in 1738; the Portuguese dossier lists only the 1783 return of Nagar Haveli. Open 'Battle of Vasai'.
- Trichinopoly 1741: the garrison and its end are on no page opened (Carnatic Sultanate, Carnatic Wars silent).
- Rohilkhand (captured 1752, devastated after 1772), the Maratha-Sikh treaty of 1785, the Treaty of Gajendragad (April 1787), the Third Anglo-Mysore War and Kharda (1795) have no ledger event: not dated or described on the pages opened. The 1780, 1783, 1792 and 1794 shape changes are therefore unexplained (unverified: page budget).
- The Baji Rao I page dates Palkhed 25 February 1728, the Maratha Empire page 28 February. The Maratha Empire page's infobox gives Pratap Singh's reign to 1818, the body to 1839; and Baji Rao II's Peshwa start as 1803 in the infobox, 1796 in the body.
- Peshwa list (Maratha Empire page): Moropant Pingle 1674-1683 (first), Balaji Vishwanath 1713-1720, Baji Rao I 1720-1740, Balaji Baji Rao 1740-1761, Madhava Rao I 1761-1772, Narayan Rao 1772-1773, Raghunath Rao 1773-1774, Sawai Madhava Rao II 1774-1795, Baji Rao II 1796-1818.

Counterparts without a dossier at writing: kolhapur-state, janjira-state, gwalior-state, indore-state, nagpur-state, satara-state, Chhatrasal (Bundelkhand), Gohad (Rana of Gohad); baroda-state (Gaekwad) is not described by the Third Anglo-Maratha War page. Gazetteer names needed: Raigad, Gingee, Karwar, Ponda, Salsette, Bassein/Vasai, Balasore, Tonk, Bundi, Rampura, Khargone, Handia (coordinates used).
